articles.title: ESPHome gives AI assistants tools to configure and install devices
articles.dek: A direct connection lets assistants create configurations, check them and run firmware builds and installations.
body: ESPHome Device Builder gives AI assistants a direct way to create and configure devices, then build and install their firmware. Its twenty tools include finding components and documentation, reading and changing configurations, checking the result and managing device automations.

J. Nick Koston connects the dashboard through Model Context Protocol, a common interface for AI tools. Long firmware jobs start separately so an assistant can check their progress or cancel them without keeping one request open.

The connection includes access to sensitive configuration: an assistant can read the secrets file. Changes to an individual secret use a dedicated action, while replacing the whole secrets file is blocked. Validation and build output conceal values marked as secrets.

articles.title: Home Assistant stops downloading the same Blink clips every five minutes
articles.dek: A repeated-media fetch consumed about 230 GB in one reported week with 14 cameras.
body: Home Assistant stops repeatedly downloading Blink motion clips it already has. One household with 14 cameras reported about 230 GB of downstream traffic in a week because the same video files were fetched again at every five-minute update.

The integration lets the camera library reuse its cached media instead of forcing a fresh download. Camera state still refreshes on the existing five-minute schedule; the change removes the repeated transfer without lengthening that interval. Dex makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction.

pullRequests.title: Stop forcing the Blink refresh on every poll

articles.title: Home Assistant brings the day’s energy picture to Apple Watch
articles.dek: A watch-face panel combines daily figures with a compact chart for each connected home.
body: Home Assistant adds a rectangular Apple Watch complication showing the home’s daily energy figures and a compact stacked chart. The app offers one panel for each connected server, using the energy dashboard configuration already in place.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves carries the phone’s Energy widget calculations onto the watch, including its early-morning fallback to yesterday’s figures. Watch faces that limit colors use different strengths of their accent color to distinguish the chart’s series.

pullRequests.title: Add an energy complication for Apple Watch

articles.title: Home Assistant restores fresh locations from iCloud devices
articles.dek: Trackers could stay frozen for hours while battery readings continued to update.
body: Home Assistant restores location updates for iCloud devices whose coordinates could remain frozen long after they moved. The integration explicitly asks Apple to locate the devices before reading their status, using its existing polling schedule.

Radek Piekarz verified the correction on an account with nine devices: one phone had kept the same coordinates for about ten hours across two trips, then moved to its actual zone on the next poll. Fresh battery readings could hide the stalled locations. Piekarz makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction.

pullRequests.title: Fix iCloud device tracker stale location by requesting an active locate on each poll

articles.title: Music Assistant restores sound on standalone HomePods running OS 27
articles.dek: Its AirPlay sender follows the speaker’s clock when a HomePod accepts playback but stays silent.
body: Music Assistant’s AirPlay sender corrects a failure that left standalone HomePods running OS 27 silent while the interface showed music playing. Those speakers insist on supplying the timing clock themselves; following it restores sound. HomePods in stereo pairs or Apple TV groups already worked.

Vincent (Chin-Chen) Lin tested the change on a first-generation HomePod running OS 27.0 with Music Assistant 2.10.3, alongside a HomePod mini in an Apple TV group. It is his first contribution to the AirPlay sender, reviewed by Marcel van der Veldt.
Van der Veldt extends the correction to setups sharing one timing service among five to eight standalone HomePods, where the extra speakers would otherwise remain silent.

Keep more than four HomePods in sync in shared PTP mode

articles.title: Music Assistant lines up announcements across speaker groups
articles.dek: Groups use a synchronized stream when their speakers cannot coordinate native announcement playback.
body: An announcement sent to a group of Home Assistant Voice speakers could reach each room at a different moment, making the message hard to understand. Music Assistant routes the clip through the group’s synchronized stream when the speakers cannot arrange a shared start themselves.

Marcel van der Veldt applies that route to Home Assistant players, ESPHome Sendspin players, Snapcast, Bose and Samsung, and to groups mixing providers. Music stops and resumes around the announcement. AirPlay and Sonos groups keep their native announcement path because those speakers can coordinate the start.

pullRequests.title: Fix announcements on a speaker group playing out of sync

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps faulty Matter reports from disrupting every device
articles.dek: Invalid fan-speed and light-brightness ranges fall back to usable defaults instead of restarting the integration.
body: A Matter fan reporting zero available speeds, or a light reporting an impossible brightness range, could interrupt Home Assistant’s connection to all its Matter devices. The integration guards those values instead of letting a calculation failure stop its listener and trigger a reload.

Franck Nijhof keeps the default speed count for an unusable fan report and the standard brightness range for an invalid light report. This extends earlier protection for invalid switch events and light color modes.

articles.title: Home Assistant repairs shortcuts shared between Apple devices
articles.dek: A shortcut shared through iCloud can use the sole configured server when its saved identity is unfamiliar.
body: A Home Assistant shortcut copied between Apple devices through iCloud could fail with “No server provided” even while displaying the right server name. The Apple app resolves an unfamiliar saved identifier to the sole configured server, keeping the same shortcut usable on both devices. Multiple-server setups and widgets keep strict matching.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves also makes newly added servers use Home Assistant’s own identity when it can be obtained through local discovery or the companion-app interface. That covers typed addresses and invitations, including remote connections when the server supplies the identity. Existing saved identifiers stay unchanged.

articles.title: Home Assistant gives Canadian automations a closer look at incoming rain
articles.dek: A new action returns radar-based precipitation estimates and hourly forecasts for custom cards and automations.
body: Home Assistant’s Environment Canada integration gains an action for detailed precipitation forecasts. It returns a six-minute series combining observed radar with roughly the next hour’s extrapolation, alongside hourly amounts, probabilities and precipitation types extending up to 48 hours.

Michael Davie exposes the data on request so a custom card or automation can choose the forecast window it needs. The action returns the provider’s series directly; it does not add a ready-made forecast display to the standard weather card.

articles.title: ESPHome stops network time from trapping ESP32-C2 devices in reboot loops
articles.dek: A startup log message could crash the device repeatedly and leave it in safe mode.
body: An ESP32-C2 configured to get the time from a network server could crash on every startup and enter safe mode after ten attempts. Jonathan Swoboda fixes the text formatter that misread the time-server log message, giving the chip the same formatter used by other ESP32 variants. J. Nick Koston reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: [esp32] Disable newlib nano printf formatting on ESP32-C2

articles.title: ESPHome keeps an alternate secrets file out of shareable history
articles.dek: Device Builder recognizes secrets.yml as well as secrets.yaml when starting a configuration repository.
body: ESPHome Device Builder keeps secrets.yml out of a configuration’s initial Git history, closing a gap that could put credentials in a repository later pushed elsewhere. It previously recognized only the longer secrets.yaml filename.
J. Nick Koston applies the same recognition to the confirmation before wiping the secrets file. Both accepted filenames receive the same protection.

pullRequests.title: Treat both secrets spellings as the secrets file

articles.title: Assist understands half-hour timers in Malayalam
articles.dek: Quarter, half and three-quarter durations join more natural ways to ask for a timer.
body: Malayalam speakers gain ways to set Assist timers using quarter, half and three-quarter durations. The sentence rules interpret fractions of an hour as minutes and fractions of a minute as seconds, and the spoken confirmation reflects the requested duration.

Arun S. Sekher also expands timer-setting phrases, native timer names and alternative number words from one through ten. The additions extend existing Malayalam timer controls rather than introducing timers to the language for the first time.

articles.title: Home Assistant actions can offer a direct photo upload
articles.dek: Blueprint and action authors gain an image field that opens the phone’s photo picker.
body: Home Assistant lets blueprint and action authors offer an image-upload field directly in their forms. On a phone, that field opens the device’s photo picker instead of requiring someone to find the media browser’s upload controls first.

The change exposes an upload option already used by picture-card editors to YAML-defined action fields and blueprint inputs. Authors must specify the accepted file types, and the paired interface change lets a chosen image be cleared so another can be uploaded. Brandon makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the change.

The foundation is looking forward to multiple days of unconference sessions and team building activities.
